title: Winter Games
build: Epyx original, PAL, two disk sides (C64 Preservation Project, verified dump)

records.c: Biathlon starts here, as Hot Dog does: interrupts off, the stack reset, $083D set to say the menu was loaded over, the BASIC ROM banked out ($01 = $26), bitmap mode with multicolour in the video chip's bank 2 ($8000-$BFFF), the CIAs' interrupts and timers off, port A of CIA 1 set to input, black border and background, and the raster interrupt at line 250 through the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at bi_irq. It also sets $15 to $40, which the zero-page clear at the start of the run undoes.

The raster interrupt, twice a frame. At line 241 it switches to text mode with the character set at $9800 (the ROM's upper and lower case set), so the bottom row is text; the next interrupt is at line 251.

At line 251: bitmap mode and multicolour again for the course, or, once the score is shown ($1E set), text mode stays and the background turns light blue. Then a step of the sound engine (sound_step), the joystick (read_stick), the next interrupt at line 241, and the frame flag at $10.
Acknowledges the raster interrupt, restores the registers the KERNAL's handler saved, and returns.

The joystick into $2D, its bits turned over so a set bit is a direction held (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, $10 fire): port 2 with one joystick ($087D) or for odd-numbered players, port 1 for the others.
Sounds stopped, the first player; then the main loop, once a frame: by the state in $11, set up the course (bi_setup), ski it (bi_frame), or after it (bi_after).
An RTS nothing reaches.
After the course. In practice ($081D negative) "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20 with YES or NO beside it: up chooses YES, down NO, fire confirms; YES skis the course again, NO goes back to the menu.
Fire on the play-again question: YES (the Y at $83E0) sets state 0 for another go; NO falls to the exit.
State 0: the course is set up again on the next frame.
In competition: the next player ($70 counts from 1 to the number of players in $081E, $72 steps through their 32-byte records), one go each; after the last, back to the menu.
Back to the menu: the stack reset and the loader's $0900, which loads the menu and starts it where it left off.
The question and its two answers for print_bottom, each a column then the text and a zero: "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20, "YES   " and "NO    " at column 32.
Prints a string on the bottom text row ($83C0): its first byte is the column, then the characters (ASCII, which the ROM's second set shows as capitals) to a zero.
The player's name and country (16 characters from the player's record at $0800 + $72) at the left of the bottom row, and spaces to its end.
Unpacks each stream in the list at ($16), two bytes an address, to a zero.

Unpacks one stream at ($14), the format of the opening ceremony's and Hot Dog's pictures: a destination address, then commands of one byte, the top two bits the kind and the low six a count (0 for 64): 0, the next byte repeated; 1, that many bytes copied; 2, that many bytes skipped; 3, that many bytes each followed by two zeros. A zero byte ends it.
The stream's end.
Steps the destination at $12-$13.
Steps the source at $14-$15.
The bridge over the stream, packed for unpack_stream: the bitmap of the top 21 rows ($A000-$BA3F), its first kilobyte filling rows 0 to 3.
The bridge's bitmap from row 3 to row 6.
The bridge's bitmap from row 6 to row 10.
The bridge's bitmap from row 10 to row 14.
The bridge's bitmap from row 14 to row 20, the bridge and the stream.
The bridge's packed bitmap, its last 140 bytes.
The bridge's screen colours, packed, to $8000-$8347.
The bridge's colour RAM, packed, to $D800-$DB47.

State 0, the course set up: the screen blanked, multicolour sprites and their colours, the rifle's sight copied into sprite shape $2F ($8BC0), zero page $10-$6F cleared, the heart drawn, the panel at the bottom unpacked (pictures, list 7), the shots left, a pulse of 60, the skier's first frame, and the first screen (next_screen). Then it waits, the water running, for the stick left or right, and sets state 1.
The sprites' colours for $D025-$D02E: yellow and grey shared by the multicolour sprites, then grey and orange in turn.

State 1, a frame of the race: the clock (clock_tick) and the heart (heart_beat); at a range, the rifle (range_frame); on the course, the drag (drag), the speed bar, the skier moved (move_skier) and stepped (ski_step), the finish line checked, the stick kept in $2C for the next frame, and the water animated on a flat screen.
The water's animation (water_step), on the flat screens only.

The next screen of the course: the screen blanked, sounds stopped, the terrain's script made to start again, and the counts of screens ($2C6D) and of the lap's screens ($51) stepped. When the lap's count reaches 7 it is a range: range_setup, and two return addresses dropped to go straight back to the main loop.
Otherwise that screen's picture from its list in pictures (8 bytes each), and its terrain from screen_types; a flat screen starts the water's sound (4) and its animation.

The skier at the left edge with the sprites' high X bits and priority cleared. Screen 31 has the finish sign drawn (draw_finish); screen 0, the first, the skier at X 48 with a full stroke's power ready and the start sign (draw_start).
The sprites on, placed, the player's name, the fresh-screen flag ($52) and the screen on.

The screens of the course passed, ranges included, from 0: the ranges are the 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th, and the finish is on screen 31. The first lap has seven screens before its range, the others six, since range_setup sets the lap's count back to 0.
The current screen's terrain: 0 flat, 1 flat then up a hill at the right, 2 down a hill then flat.
The terrain of each of the seven screens of a lap, by $51: flat, down, up, flat, down, up, flat.
On screen 31 with the skier at X 232 or more: a pause of 90 frames, the score (show_score), in competition a pause of 30 frames and fire, and state 2.

The skier's X ($34-$36, a fraction and nine bits) moved on by the speed ($37-$38). Past X 320 the next screen; otherwise the skier's Y and the terrain from the screen's type and X: flat at line 130; type 1 flat at line 148 until X 198, then climbing a line for each four pixels; type 2 down a line for each four pixels from line 111 until X 250, then flat at line 171.
The terrain's drag into $41, from terrain_drag.
Puts the skier's eight sprites in a block of two by two, each place two sprites over each other, at X $35-$36 and Y $3A.
The sprite pointers for the frame shown, shapes $4F to $4F+7, the multicolour sprite of each place the even shape and the hires one over it the odd.
The skier's step. A change of terrain starts its script (ski_scripts). Otherwise, while the frame's time in $40 runs, a stroke can cut it short; when it is $FF or $FE the skier waits for a stroke.

Waiting for a stroke: the stick must have been let go since the last ($2C clear, or a fresh screen) and pushed now in the terrain's direction (stroke_dirs). A stroke on a slope sounds (3), raises the pulse, and adds the power built up while waiting ($43) to the speed, to at most 512; then the script's next frame.
The first frame of a wait, $FF, becomes $FE.
No stroke yet: the stroke's power in $43 grows by the terrain's step in power_steps, up to its limit in power_limits.
How fast the power of a stroke builds while the skier waits, by terrain: 8 a frame on the flat, 254 at once uphill, 31 downhill.
The power's limits, by terrain: 113 on the flat, 255 uphill, 193 downhill.
The drag taken off the speed each frame, by terrain: 2 on the flat, 12 uphill, 1 downhill.
The frame's time running: a stroke now, after the stick has been let go, goes straight to the next frame with a rise in pulse; otherwise the time counts down.
The script's next frame: its time into $40, then the frame shown; a frame number of $FF goes back by the next byte, to loop.
The stick direction that makes a stroke, by terrain: left or right on the flat and uphill, down on the downhill, poling with both arms.
The three terrains' scripts.
The scripts' addresses' high bytes, read one on from ski_scripts.
The addresses of the skier's 16 frames, at $9000-$9DA6.
The frames' addresses' high bytes, read one on from frame_table.
The flat's script: frame 0, wait for a stroke, frames 1 and 2 for ten frames each, frame 3, wait, frames 4 and 5, and round again: the diagonal stride.
Uphill: the same with frames 10 to 15.
Downhill: frame 8, the poles planted, waiting; a stroke gives frames 7 and 6, the push with both poles, frame 9, the tuck, for 15 frames, then 6 and 7 back up.
The terrain's drag taken off the speed each frame, down to 0.
Steps the script pointer at $3E-$3F.
A stroke raises the pulse ($4C-$4D) by a 32nd of what it lacks of 140, twice on an uphill.
One rise of the pulse: a 32nd of the difference between 140 and the pulse added to it.

Unpacks the skier's frame Y into the sprite shapes not on screen, $8C00 (shapes $30-$37) or $8E00 ($38-$3F), and makes those the next shown. A frame is 64 groups of eight bytes: a mask byte, then the bytes its set bits stand for, the clear ones zero.

The packed pictures' lists for unpack_list, eight bytes each: the bitmap, the screen's colours and the colour RAM of the top 21 rows. Three scenes in turn for the seven screens of a lap: the bridge over the stream ($1274), the downhill past the hut ($48CB) and the climb ($31D6); the eighth list is the panel at the bottom ($4613), drawn once.

The score at the end: sounds stopped, the sprites off, the tune (sound 0), the score screen unpacked in text mode (score_list), the skiing time, the misses and five seconds for each, and the total, which goes into the player's record.
The misses as one or two digits, before "MISSES".
The penalty, five seconds a miss, as minutes and seconds in $18-$1B.
The total: the clock's digits added to the penalty's, each carried at its limit (score_limits); a total that passes 99:59 shows 99:59.
The total written as text into the player's record (offsets $10-$15), and as the score at $16-$18 with its digits turned over, so that a shorter time is a bigger number for the menu's sorting.
Each digit's limit for the carry: 10, 10, 6, 10.
Prints four digits from ($16) at ($14) on the text screen as "mm:ss", a leading zero shown as a space.
Steps the screen pointer at $14-$15.
The score screen's two streams for unpack_list: its text and its colours.
The score screen's text, packed: "BIATHLON SCORE", "TOTAL SKIING TIME", "MISSES X 5 SECS", a line and "TOTAL TIME", to $8000-$83BF.
Its colours, packed, to $D800-$DBBD.
The rifle's sight, a ring with a cross in it, as sprite shape $2F.
The value of a digit character, a space counting 0.
The climb, the third scene, packed: its bitmap, the first kilobyte filling rows 0 to 4.
The climb's bitmap from row 4 to row 8.
The climb's bitmap from row 8 to row 12.
The climb's bitmap from row 12 to row 20, the slope.
The climb's packed bitmap from $4000 on.
The climb's screen colours, packed.
The climb's colour RAM, packed, to $D800-$DB47.
The panel at the bottom, packed: bitmap rows 21 to 24 ($BA40-$BF3F) with SPEED, TIME, HIT, MISS, SHOTS and PULSE.
The panel's screen colours, packed, to $8348-$83E7.
Its colour RAM, packed, to $DB48-$DBE7.
The downhill past the hut, the second scene, packed: its bitmap, the first kilobyte filling rows 0 to 4.
The downhill's bitmap from row 4 to row 9.
The downhill's bitmap from row 9 to row 13.
The downhill's bitmap from row 13 to row 20, the slope.
The downhill's screen colours, packed.
The downhill's colour RAM, packed, to $D800-$DB47.
The shooting range, packed: the five targets on their board between the trees. Its bitmap, the first kilobyte filling rows 0 to 3.
The range's bitmap from row 3 to row 7, the targets' board.
The range's bitmap from row 7 to row 11.
The range's bitmap from row 11 to row 20, the snow in front.
The range's packed bitmap, its last 50 bytes.
The range's screen colours, packed.
The range's colour RAM, packed, to $D800-$DB47.

A shooting range: its picture (range_list), every sprite off but the sight, the skier stopped, the lap's count of screens back to 0, the rifle empty, "EMPTY" on the bottom row, the sight on the first target, and the bitmap address of the first target in $3E-$3F.
A frame at the range: the sight moved (sight_move) and the rifle (rifle).
The sight's height: as each beat of the heart comes it is thrown up to line 88 with a falling speed that grows with the pulse (sight_speeds); between beats it falls by that speed.

The rifle, by its state in rifle_state: empty, the stick down opens the bolt (sound 6, "BOLT OPEN"); open, up loads it (sound 7, "LOADED"); loaded, a fresh press of fire shoots (sound 5) and it is empty again.
The stick kept in $2C for the next frame.

A shot hits when the sight is at lines 113 to 117: the hits ($22) or the misses ($23) counted and drawn on the panel, and a hit target drawn as hit. The shots left drawn, a pause of six frames, and the sight moved on eight pixels to the next target; after the fifth, a pause of 30 frames and the course again.
The range's picture, packed, for unpack_list: bitmap, screen colours and colour RAM.
The bitmap of a target hit, five bytes, for the last target.
The same for the other four.
"  EMPTY  " for the bottom row at column 25, as a stream for unpack_stream.
"BOLT OPEN", the same.
" LOADED  ", the same.
The rifle: 0 empty, 1 the bolt open, 2 loaded.

Each frame: the pulse eased down (pulse_down), and the heart's count run down. At its end, between beats: the heart drawn small with the beat's thump (sound 1) for 10 frames. At the end of those: the heart big for the frames to the next beat, from heart_table by the pulse.
The pulse eased down by 6/256 a frame to its rest at 60, and its number on the panel redrawn when it changes.
The small heart, drawn for the 10 frames of each beat, for the panel's bitmap: its top 24 bytes at $BB60.
The small heart's bottom 24 bytes, at $BCA0.
The big heart, drawn between beats, top half.
The big heart's bottom half.
1 while the heart is drawn big, between beats.
Frames to the heart's next change.
For each pulse from 60 to 140, two at a time, four bytes: the frames between beats (50 at 60, 15 at 140), a zero, and the sight's falling speed (from 170/256 to 398/256 of a line a frame).
The sight's falling speeds, the third and fourth bytes of heart_table's entries, read through this address.
Their high bytes.
Draws the number in $16 at the bitmap address in $14-$15 with the panel's digits, right-aligned in three cells.
Copies a digit's five bytes of bitmap from digits into the cell at ($14).
Moves ($14) to the next character cell, eight bytes on.
The shots left, 20 less the hits and the misses, drawn on the panel.
The water under the bridge: every four to eight frames, at random, the next of three pictures of its flow copied into two rows of the bitmap.
Which of the three pictures is next.
Frames to the next change.
The start sign, eight characters by five, copied from sign_start into the bitmap, its screen colours and colour RAM set.
The finish sign, seven by five, from sign_finish.
Copies a sign of five rows, X bytes of bitmap each, from ($16) to ($14), with the colours $12 and $0F in the screen and colour RAM at ($18) and ($1A).

The race clock, a frame at a time in six digits ($24-$29): frames, tenths, seconds, tens of seconds, minutes, tens of minutes, each carried at its limit in clock_limits. It stops at 99:59.9. Six frames make a tenth, right for an NTSC machine's 60 frames a second; a PAL machine has 50, so its clock runs a fifth slow.
The clock's digits' limits: 10, 10, 6, 10, 10, 6, tens of minutes first.
Draws clock digit X on the panel, but for the frames.
Where on the panel the clock's five shown digits go.
The clock's places' high bytes, read one on.
The speed bar on the panel: the speed in 16ths, at most 30, drawn as full cells of four and a part cell from bar_parts, the rest cleared.
A part cell of the speed bar, 0 to 4.
The panel's digits 0 to 9, five bytes of bitmap each.
A decimal point's five bytes, which nothing reads.
The three pictures of the water's flow, each 104 bytes for one row of the bitmap and 104 for the next.
The first picture of the water, its second row.
The second picture of the water, its first row.
The second picture, its second row.
The third picture of the water, its first row.
The third picture, its second row.
An unused entry to wait_frames, LDX #60: a second's wait, which nothing calls.
Waits X frames.
Waits X frames, then until fire is pressed.
Waits for the interrupt's frame flag at $10, then steps the random number.
The random number at $7751-$7753, 24 bits with the high byte first, shifted right once, the bit fed in at the top the exclusive or of the low byte's bits 0 and 5.
The random number's three bytes.
Its middle byte.
Its low byte, whose bits 0 and 5 make the next bit.

The sound engine's six slots, 32 bytes each, a sound playing in each: +0 the SID voice it plays on (0 to 2), bit 7 set when the slot is idle; +1-2 the script's address; +3 the frames until its next step; +4 a loop count; +5-6 its return stack's pointer; +8 to +14 its copy of the voice's seven registers (frequency, pulse width, control, attack-decay, sustain-release); +15 a flag that restarts the envelope; +16 its transposition; +17 a fine tuning; +18-21 a frequency slide (step, count, rate); +22-25 a pulse-width sweep (step, period, count). The file holds leftover bytes here, which stop_all clears.
Slot 0's script address (+1 and +2), the base start_sound writes each slot's through.
The script address's high byte.
Slot 0's count of frames to its next step (+3).
Slot 0's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep (+16 to +25), which start_sound clears for the slot it starts.
Slots 2 and 3.
Slots 4 and 5.
The slot count of sound_step's loops.
One byte for each SID voice: set once a slot has written the voice this frame, so a slot numbered higher wins a voice over a lower one.
Voice 1's claim.
Voice 2's claim.
Nonzero while the engine runs; start_sound clears it while it writes a slot.
The filter's registers, copied to $D415-$D418 every frame: the cutoff's low and high bytes, the resonance and the voices filtered, the filter mode and the volume.
The cutoff's high byte, for $D416.
The resonance and the voices filtered, for $D417.
The filter mode and the volume, for $D418.
The six slots' return stacks for the scripts' calls, 16 bytes each.
start_sound's copies of X and Y.
start_sound's copy of Y.
Three bytes nothing reads.
The counters of the two arpeggio routines at $7B14 and $7B36, which nothing calls.
The second arpeggio routine's counter.
The S key's switch: a press sets it to 1 when it is 0, and clears it, stopping every sound, when it is not; nothing else reads it. The file holds $FE here, so the first press stops the sounds.

Starts sound A (100 and above are ignored) from snd_table: its first byte is the slot it plays in, its second the SID voice; the slot's script starts at its third byte on the next step, with the slot's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep cleared. A sound already playing in that slot is cut off.
Steps the slot pointer at $80-$81; nothing calls it.
Steps the script pointer at $82-$83.
Steps the pointer at $86-$87 through a sound's first bytes.
The S key's debounce count, 0 to 2.

The sound engine, once a frame from the interrupt. First the S key, read through CIA 1 (row 1, column 5): pressed after a release, it turns snd_s_key over. The event's start-up makes port A of CIA 1 an input (it writes 0 to $DC02), so the engine's write there drives no row; the key is seen only while joystick 2 is held down, which pulls row 1 low on the same line.
For each of the six slots that is not idle: the frequency slide (snd_slide), the pulse-width sweep, and, when its count of frames runs out, the next step of its script (script_step).
The slide: the rate taken from the count, and the step added to the frequency when it passes zero.

The pulse-width sweep: every frame the step is added to the pulse width, and turned round each time the period runs out. A slip makes it change only the width's low byte: the high byte's add goes to the low byte too, with no INY between.
The slot's frames counted down; at zero its script runs on.

Copies the slots to the SID, from slot 5 down to 0: each voice takes the registers of the highest slot that plays on it, and a slot's restart flag turns the gate off and on again to restart the envelope. Then the filter's four registers.
The SID's three voices' register addresses, $D400, $D407 and $D40E.
The voices' register addresses' high bytes, read one on from sid_voices.
Stops every sound: the slots and their stacks cleared, each slot idle with its stack pointer set, volume 15 with the low-pass mode and nothing filtered, and the SID's voice registers cleared.
The six slots' stack addresses.
Writes 0 to the SID's registers $D400-$D415.
An arpeggio: sets the slot's transposition from the next of 16 steps in snd_arp_table_one. Nothing calls it.
Its 16 transpositions in semitones.
Another, for two slots side by side, from snd_arp_table_two. Nothing calls it either.
Its 16 transpositions.

Runs a slot's script from ($82) until it waits. A byte under $80 is a note: its pitch (set_note), then a byte of how many frames it lasts, and the gate on with the envelope restarted. From $80 a command, its number in the low seven bits, through snd_commands; numbers above 28 stop the sound (cmd_stop).
Steps past a command's last byte and runs the next.
An RTS after snd_continue that nothing reaches.
A note: its pitch, its length, the gate on.
Steps past the length, then sets the restart flag and the gate on.

The 29 commands' routines: 0 set the loop count, 1 loop to an address while the count lasts, 2 start another sound, 3 call machine code, 4 jump to an address, 5 call a part of a script, 6 return from it, 7 end, 8 stop, 9 transpose, 10 tune, 11 jump to machine code, 12 a note with a pulse width, 13 a tied note (no new envelope), 14 the gate off for a time, 15 attack-decay and sustain-release, 16 the waveform and envelope, 17 the pulse width, pulse waveform and envelope, 18 a raw frequency for a time, 19 the slide off, 20 the sweep, 21 the slide, 22 the volume, 23 the resonance, 24 the cutoff, 25 the filter mode, 26 the voices filtered, 27 cutoff, mode and resonance from three bytes, 28 cutoff, resonance and routing, and mode.
The command routines' high bytes, read one on from snd_commands.
Command 11: jumps to the machine code at the next two bytes; its RTS ends the slot's step.
Command 3: calls the machine code at the next two bytes, then goes on with the script.
Jumps through $84-$85.
Back from the machine code to the next command.
Command 7: the slot goes idle.
Command 8, and any number above 28: the slot's registers cleared, the gate left on with no waveform, and two frames later the end command at snd_end_byte.
Command 7 ($87), where cmd_stop points the script.

Sets the slot's frequency from a note byte: the high four bits the octave, the low four the semitone, plus the slot's transposition, from note_freqs shifted right once for each octave under 7; 15 gives the highest frequency, $FFFF, for noise. The slot's fine tuning is added.

The SID frequencies of 24 semitones from C in the top octave: C is $430F, which is 1046.5 Hz on an NTSC machine and two-thirds of a semitone flat on a PAL one, as in the opening ceremony's and the menu's tables.
The frequencies' high bytes, read one on from note_freqs.
Eight bytes of code nothing reaches: a read, a step and a read.
Command 16: the control byte (waveform and gate), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 17: the pulse width, then the pulse waveform with the gate ($41), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 18: a frequency of two bytes, then a length and the gate on.
A note's length, then the gate on.
Command 4: the script goes on at the next two bytes.
Command 1: the loop count less one; until it reaches 0 the script goes back to the next two bytes' address, then on past them.
Command 0: sets the loop count.
Command 2: starts another sound, often the other voices of a tune.
Command 5: pushes the address after the command onto the slot's stack and goes to the next two bytes' address.
Command 6: back to the address on the slot's stack.
Command 9: the slot's transposition, in semitones.
Command 10: the slot's fine tuning, added to every frequency.
Command 22: the volume, the low four bits of $D418.
Command 24: the filter's cutoff, high byte.
Command 25: the filter mode, the high four bits of $D418.
Command 26: which voices go through the filter, the low four bits of $D417.
Command 23: the resonance, the high four bits of $D417.
Command 27: the cutoff from the first byte and the top bit of the second, the mode from the second's low four bits and the cutoff's low bits from its high four, then the resonance and routing.
Two bytes the filter commands work in.
The filter command's second byte, kept while it works.

Command 21: the slide's rate (255 for every frame) and its step of two bytes, added to the frequency at that rate: the rate is taken from a count each frame, and each time the count passes zero the step is added.
Command 20: the sweep's period and its step.
A note command no table entry reaches: pitch, length, gate.
Command 13: a new pitch and length with no new envelope, the notes tied.
A pulse-width command no table entry reaches.
Command 15: attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 14: the gate off, and a wait of the next byte's frames.
Command 12: a note with the pulse width's high byte, then its length.
Command 19: the slide stopped.
Command 28: the cutoff's high byte, the resonance and routing, and the mode.
The addresses of the event's 12 sounds, by number, for start_sound. Each is a slot, a SID voice and a script.
The sounds' addresses' high bytes, read one on from snd_table.
Three bytes between the table and the sounds that nothing reads.
Sound 7, the rifle loaded: a click of voice 0's pulse, with sounds 9 and 6.
Sound 9, under the loading: a frequency slide on voice 2 with bit 7 of $D418 set, which takes voice 3 out of the output unless the filter routes it.
Sound 6, the bolt opened, and part of the loading: a short burst of noise on voice 1.
Sound 4, the stream: noise through the band-pass filter on voice 2, held round and round while the screen is flat.
Sound 5, a shot: low-passed noise, with sound 8.
Sound 8, the shot's crack on voice 0: a short noise.
Sound 3, a stroke on a slope: a burst of noise through the band-pass, then a sweep down through the high-pass.
Sound 2, a short pulse blip on voice 1, which nothing starts.
Sound 1, the heart's thump: a low triangle note sliding down, twice.
Sound 11, the tune's melody on voice 2, sawtooth: long notes, round and round.
Sound 0, the score screen's tune: voice 0's short triangle notes on a steady beat, which starts sounds 10 and 11 for the other voices.
Sound 10, the tune's bass on voice 1: a long pulse note with its width swept, round and round.
Frame 0 of the skier, for draw_frame: the diagonal stride on the flat, poles back.
Frame 1, the stride.
Frame 2, the stride, legs together.
Frame 3, the other leg's stride, pole planted.
Frame 4, the stride.
Frame 5, the stride, legs together.
Frame 6, downhill: pushing with both poles.
Frame 7, downhill: the poles swinging forward.
Frame 8, downhill: upright with the poles planted.
Frame 9, downhill: the tuck.
Frame 10, uphill: the stride on the slope.
Frame 11, uphill.
Frame 12, uphill.
Frame 13, uphill, the other leg.
Frame 14, uphill.
Frame 15, uphill.
The finish sign, five rows of 56 bytes of bitmap (seven characters), for draw_finish.
The start sign, five rows of 64 bytes (eight characters), for draw_start; its last byte is the file's last, $9FFE.
